correctness.rationale: Exact explicit GP(8,3) edge set. Enumerate every nonempty 16-vertex mask; forbidden connected triples (48) and an independent induced-component traversal agree on all 65,535 masks and yield 6,812 nonempty faces. The specified 16-pivot staged face matching has exactly 3,404 disjoint matched Hasse pairs and critical masks 8192,33637,33644,49964, in dimensions 0,6,6,6. The verifier constructs all 35,104 directed Hasse incidences, reverses precisely matching edges and exhaustively sorts all 6,812 vertices; hence the matching is acyclic. Forman gives a CW complex with one 0-cell and three 6-cells and no intervening cells, and therefore the integral wedge of three S^6. Auxiliary mod-two boundary reduction independently yields beta_6=3; this is not substituted for integral homotopy.

originality.rationale: Fresh source Sawant, arXiv:2605.25150v1, identifies 3-path-free with 2-independence and classifies tree complexes, but the Möbius–Kantor graph has cycles and its homotopy type is not determined. Deshpande–Singh 2001.05448v2 and Deshpande–Shukla–Singh 2001.06775v1 cover other graph families or general bounds. The complete public mathematical records with the same graph concern ordinary edge-forbidding independence and a total cut complex, whose face definitions do not imply the 2-independence classification. Alias/parameter searches in published-finding corpus, mathematical primary literature and own accessible ledger found no equivalent or dominating result. The conclusion is a best-evidence priority judgment, not a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is the classical symmetric cubic 16-vertex generalized Petersen/Levi graph, not an arbitrary slice. The two-independence complex is the first natural higher-independence step and the 3-path-free complex emphasized in the recent motivating literature. Its complete integral homotopy is a meaningful nonchordal benchmark, contrasting with the separately computed mixed-dimensional ordinary independence homotopy for the same graph. The exact three six-spheres are not fixed by existing general bounds and can serve as a reproducible reference example; a family theorem is not claimed or needed.
